topic: Support-adaptive uniform joint inference for the accepted survivor-complier sharp benefit interval. Keep the accepted parent's finite-X, finite-ordered-Y binary-IV model and exact endpoint map Phi=(L,U), assume only instrument overlap and aggregate survivor mass M>=m_*>0, and allow individual survivor cells and threshold gaps to vanish arbitrarily. Construct the explicit nearby-legal-base directional envelope T_n and its common-Gaussian max-norm rectangle C_n. Prove uniform joint 1-alpha coverage over all triangular arrays, exact oracle Gaussian calibration on separated regular faces, and O_P(n^-1/2) width along root-n emerging-support and tied-cut arrays. The hard kernel is the legal observed-law inner-neighborhood comparison and relative critical-value transfer when endpoint variance vanishes; pointwise bootstrap validity, endpoint-wise Bonferroni, or the parent's deterministic guard cannot substitute. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: the presolve derived the finite unconditional-capacity reduction, regular-face oracle calibration, uniformly tight critical values, and a multinomial Gaussian coupling. It verified a legal K=4 two-cell array with upper cuts (.40,.30,.30,.40), M_n=.25+.25/sqrt(n), exact upper endpoint (.8+.4/sqrt(n))/(1+1/sqrt(n)), and centered limit N(0,1.28); a Poisson rare-outcome counterexample attempt was conservatively covered by endogenous nearby-base padding. These calculations separate root-n deterministic drift from sampling fluctuation and correctly type projection on contrast masses rather than atom vectors. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: prove the deterministic inner-neighborhood comparison LC, especially legal-law realization of capacity derivative domination and relative quantile validity when the envelope scale vanishes. EARLY KILL TEST: certify legal-face maximization on K=4 two-cell arrays combining root-n survivor emergence, lambda/n rare atoms, simultaneous ties, and a degenerate endpoint limit for a_n=n^-1/3 and n^-0.49; a controlled coverage deficit or persistent legal-versus-ambient mismatch stops the run. open_problems.open_problem: Does the finite binary-IV survivor-complier observed-law model admit a uniform inner-neighborhood realization theorem showing that every capacity-envelope direction relevant to Phi is dominated by directions generated by nearby legal multinomial laws, including at zero cells, simultaneous active-cut ties, and degenerate endpoint faces?

source_refs.claim: Shows that high-level geometric assumptions used for inference in partially identified models are constraint qualifications whose verification can be stringent and model-specific.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido, Francesca Molinari, Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Obtains pointwise root-n LP-value inference but proves that uniform consistency is impossible without restrictions on the underlying distribution class.
source_refs.author: Andrei Voronin

source_refs.claim: Represents discrete causal bounds as optimization over admissible data-generating processes and identifies uncertainty quantification for complex discrete bounds as an outstanding direction.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: For the converse, we construct an exact-local, causal-realizable, common-support submodel.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic directional-delta and LP-value results perturb an ambient parameter or impose a constraint qualification, whereas the required comparison must stay inside the causal observed-law image: nonnegative atom probabilities, normalization, binary-IV compatibility, overlap, and survivor/complier restrictions must be jointly realizable. At a zero cell the ambient tangent cone may strictly exceed the cone generated by legal submodels, while tied cuts can activate several capacity directions simultaneously. Kaido–Molinari–Stoye explain why this geometry cannot be assumed, Voronin shows why unrestricted uniform LP inference is impossible, and Duarte et al. optimize over legal causal models without proving the local realization needed here. The prior CausalSmith construction supplies an exact-local, causal-realizable common-support template, but its first proof step must be replaced by an explicit realization of prescribed capacity perturbations inside the binary-IV compatibility polytope.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive legal-tangent and inner-cone comparison lemma mapping every candidate endpoint-envelope direction to O(t)-nearby admissible observed laws and proving uniform two-sided derivative domination for L and U over M>=m_*, or a finite K=4 counterexample locating the boundary regime where domination fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing keeps admissible causal data-generating processes, rather than an unconstrained probability vector, at the center of sharp-bounds analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Discrete causal assumptions define a legal latent-law region -> sharp bounds optimize over that region -> numerical sharpness does not characterize local legal perturbations -> identify the legal tangent geometry required for uniform survivor-complier endpoint inference

method_exemplars.technique: Translate regularity assumptions into tangent-cone and Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualifications, then compare the resulting local feasible-direction cones using variational geometry.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is precisely an equality or domination relation between the analytically convenient envelope cone and the genuine causal-law feasible cone.

method_exemplars.technique: Regularize an LP-value estimator to accommodate solution multiplicity and overidentifying constraints, while separating fixed-law asymptotic normality from the restrictions required for uniformity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Phi is a finite optimization-value map with changing optimizers, and the sought legal inner-neighborhood condition is the model-specific restriction needed to escape unrestricted uniformity impossibility.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one common-Gaussian rectangular confidence set for the survivor-complier sharp benefit endpoints (L,U) attain uniform joint 1-alpha coverage over legal triangular arrays with vanishing cells and threshold gaps, exact oracle calibration on separated faces, and root-n width on root-n emerging-support and tied-cut arrays?

source_refs.claim: Derives sharp bounds and nonparametric efficient estimation for a survivor-complier causal effect under selection on treatment, but not ordinal benefit endpoints or support-degenerate joint inference.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Steve Harris, Luke J. Keele
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Derives sharp symbolic probability-of-benefit bounds for ordinal outcomes in imperfect randomized trials and suggests bootstrap uncertainty quantification without uniform analysis at ties or vanishing cells.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, Andreas Kryger Jensen

source_refs.claim: Provides uniformly valid simultaneous rectangles for vector-valued partially identified parameters when the lower- and upper-bound estimators already have an asymptotically normal representation.
source_refs.author: Brigham R. Frandsen, Zachari A. Pond

source_refs.excerpt: Derive a dependent growing-window process approximation ... retaining selection and truncation bias

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest literatures stop on different sides of the target: Kennedy–Harris–Keele supply the survivor-complier population and fixed-law inference, Gabriel–Sachs–Jensen supply ordinal benefit bounds, and Frandsen–Pond supply joint rectangles only after asymptotic normality of all endpoint estimators is available. Here Phi is a max/min capacity map whose active affine piece changes at ties, while disappearing survivor cells can collapse endpoint-envelope variances. The prior POMDP proposal isolates the analogous failure of a fixed-score CLT after selecting a tuning representation; transferring that construction requires replacing the history-indexed process by the finite legal directional-envelope process and retaining all support/tie selections before Gaussian approximation. Consequently, neither pointwise influence functions, the ordinary bootstrap, nor endpoint-wise Bonferroni establishes the requested triangular-array result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit nearby-legal-base directional statistic T_n and conditional common-Gaussian max-norm rectangle C_n, with a theorem proving uniform joint 1-alpha coverage, exact oracle Gaussian equivalence on separated regular faces, and O_P(n^-1/2) coordinate widths along the specified emerging-support and tie arrays.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly motivates why standard IV effects cease to be meaningful under selection and introduces the survivor-complier population before deriving sharp bounds and inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Selection makes outcomes or treatments undefined for some units -> the standard IV estimand loses its causal interpretation -> sharp survivor-complier bounds restore a meaningful target -> obtain honest joint inference when the benefit interval's support and active cuts are unstable

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the Hadamard directional derivative and resample that derivative applied to a Gaussian empirical-process draw; the proof combines a directional delta method with conditional weak convergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint map is piecewise smooth, so its tied-face limit is a nonlinear directional transform of a Gaussian score rather than an ordinary linear influence-function limit.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate one rectangular critical value from the joint Gaussian covariance of estimated lower and upper bounds to obtain simultaneous point coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested output is a joint rectangle for two bound endpoints, but its Gaussian input must be replaced by a face-adaptive directional envelope.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine scale-free Gaussian-max density and anti-concentration bounds with Gaussian or multiplier-bootstrap coupling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The common rectangle is governed by an unsigned Gaussian maximum whose coordinates inherit potentially collapsing endpoint-envelope variances.

open_problems.open_problem: Can conditional Gaussian max-norm critical values be transferred with relative rather than additive error when the entire covariance scale of a causal endpoint envelope tends to zero, without imposing a fixed lower bound on any marginal variance?

source_refs.claim: Provides scale-free density and anti-concentration bounds for centered Gaussian maxima, including an unsigned-max extension, but its stated uniform bootstrap consequence anchors scale through a largest marginal variance separated from zero.
source_refs.author: Suhas Vijaykumar

source_refs.claim: Develops Gaussian and bootstrap approximation-error bounds for maxima through randomized Lindeberg interpolation under standard nondegeneracy conditions.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Kengo Kato, Yuta Koike

source_refs.claim: Obtains near-parametric bootstrap rates for maxima under weak coordinate-variance decay, using ordered variance structure rather than allowing unrestricted collapse of the common scale.
source_refs.author: Miles E. Lopes, Zhenhua Lin, Hans-Georg Müller

open_problems.why_unsolved: Coverage transfer for a shrinking rectangle requires approximation error that is small relative to the Gaussian critical radius; additive covariance or Kolmogorov error can swamp that radius when all envelope variances vanish. Vijaykumar removes dependence on the minimum coordinate variance and treats unsigned maxima, but the uniform bootstrap implication still uses a largest variance separated from zero. Variance-decay methods instead rank small coordinates relative to a nonvanishing leading block. The survivor-benefit setting permits the entire contrast process to collapse, so the missing object is a homogeneous relative comparison tied to an estimable common scale, together with a logically separate exactly-degenerate branch.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A scale-homogeneous Gaussian comparison and conditional-bootstrap quantile theorem proving q_hat/q converges to one when the true max-norm quantile q is positive under relative covariance control, plus an exact-zero rule that preserves joint endpoint coverage when q equals zero.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames small coordinate variances as an anti-concentration and bootstrap obstacle and organizes the response around scale-free Gaussian geometry.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Max-based simultaneous inference needs anti-concentration -> coordinatewise standardization becomes unstable at tiny variances -> scale-free geometry removes minimum-variance dependence -> obtain relative quantile transfer when even the largest variance vanishes

method_exemplars.technique: Control Gaussian-max density through facet geometry and the largest marginal scale, then combine the bound with Gaussian and bootstrap couplings.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint rectangle uses an unsigned maximum with heterogeneous and possibly zero coordinate variances; the proof must refine this machinery to allow collapse of the entire scale.

method_exemplars.technique: Use iterative randomized Lindeberg interpolation, smoothing, and anti-concentration to compare maxima of sums with Gaussian and bootstrap analogues.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Relative critical-value validity requires rebuilding the coupling component so every remainder scales with the collapsing envelope covariance.

method_exemplars.technique: Stratify coordinates by variance and prove that sufficiently low-variance coordinates cannot determine the maximum.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Variance stratification is the nearest existing device for controlling negligible coordinates, but it must be made relative when no fixed high-variance block remains.

open_problems.open_problem: What are the sharp separation-rate conditions under which an honest support-adaptive confidence rectangle for Phi can switch to the exact oracle bivariate-Gaussian critical value on a regular face, and is oracle adaptation impossible when active-cut gaps or endpoint standard deviations close faster than those rates?

source_refs.claim: Shows that ordinary bootstrap consistency for a directionally differentiable functional is equivalent to full differentiability under a Gaussian first stage and develops derivative-aware resampling.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang, Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Proves pointwise numerical directional-delta validity generally and uniform validity for convex Lipschitz maps.
source_refs.author: Han Hong, Jessie Li

source_refs.claim: Shows that confidence procedures for interval-identified parameters face a nuisance-boundary problem and that a purported earlier uniformity result implicitly required local superefficiency.
source_refs.author: Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Establishes exact asymptotic LP-value coverage at each fixed law but an impossibility of uniform consistency without restrictions on the law class.
source_refs.author: Andrei Voronin

open_problems.why_unsolved: Oracle calibration requires consistently learning both the active affine endpoint pieces and their effective covariance, yet near-ties make face selection statistically indistinguishable. Fang–Santos and Hong–Li handle nonsmooth delta inference but do not give a necessary-and-sufficient transition between least-favorable honesty and exact regular-face calibration for a rational sharp-bound map constrained to legal IV laws. Stoye's nuisance-boundary correction and Voronin's LP uniformity impossibility show that unrestricted adaptation cannot simply be assumed. The unresolved quantity is the joint frontier in active-cut separation, support emergence, and shrinking Gaussian scale at which oracle critical values become recoverable without losing coverage on contiguous legal arrays.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A phase-transition theorem giving sufficient gap-to-noise and variance-estimation rates for oracle-equivalent face selection and calibration, matched by contiguous legal triangular-array lower bounds or counterexamples proving incompatibility of exact oracle calibration and uniform 1-alpha coverage below those rates.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates nonsmooth inference through ordinary-bootstrap failure and identifies the derivative as the object governing both valid procedures and impossibility.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Endpoint maps are nonsmooth at tied faces -> the ordinary bootstrap misses the Gaussian-directional limit -> derivative-aware calibration restores validity -> determine when calibration can adapt back to the exact oracle Gaussian rectangle

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate a directional derivative by finite perturbation of the original functional and balance perturbation bias against first-stage stochastic error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A nearby-base implementation of Phi is a model-aware numerical directional derivative whose tuning rate should expose the same bias-to-noise boundary governing oracle face recovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Use full differentiability as the dividing line for ordinary bootstrap validity and analyze local alternatives through the directional derivative.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Separated faces make Phi differentiable, while tied faces leave a nonlinear directional derivative, matching the proposed oracle-versus-envelope transition.

method_exemplars.technique: Reparameterize interval inference around a nuisance boundary and evaluate coverage uniformly along sequences where identification width shrinks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Closing active gaps and endpoint variances play the role of shrinking-width nuisance parameters, making this a template for the lower-bound and uniform-calibration argument.

literature_map:
Kennedy, Harris & Keele (2019, JASA, arXiv:1704.05706) is the direct survivor-complier anchor: sharp bounds and efficient inference under selection on treatment.
Lu, Ding & Dasgupta (2018, JEBS, arXiv:1507.01542) derive sharp probability-of-benefit and no-harm bounds for finite ordinal outcomes, including noncompliance applications.
Lu, Zhang & Ding (2020, Biometrics, arXiv:1907.10287) sharpen related ordinal relative-treatment-effect endpoint formulas.
Gabriel, Sachs & Jensen (2024, Biometrika, arXiv:2305.10555) extend symbolic benefit bounds to imperfect randomized trials but do not develop support-degenerate uniform theory.
Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo & Shpitser (2024, JASA) reduce discrete causal bounds to optimization over legal latent laws and leave broadly valid uncertainty quantification as a further layer.
Imbens & Manski (2004, Econometrica) and Stoye (2009, Econometrica) show that even scalar interval inference has a delicate shrinking-width nuisance-boundary problem.
Romano & Shaikh (2010, Econometrica) give broad uniform inference for identified sets, generally through set procedures rather than adaptive endpoint rectangles.
Chernozhukov, Lee & Rosen (2013, Econometrica, arXiv:0907.3503) develop Gaussian-process inference and adaptive selection for intersection bounds, but not causal-law inner-neighborhood realization.
Fang & Santos (2019, ReStud, arXiv:1404.3763) establish ordinary-bootstrap failure for nonlinear directional derivatives and derivative-aware resampling.
Hong & Li (2018, Journal of Econometrics) provide a numerical directional delta method with uniform results for convex Lipschitz maps; Phi's legal rational-map geometry lies outside that result.
Firpo, Galvao & Parker (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1911.10215) develop local and some uniform inference for optimized value functions, supporting the directional-value-function connection.
Frandsen & Pond (2025, JBES) provide simultaneous rectangles for vector partially identified parameters conditional on asymptotically normal bound estimators.
Kaido, Molinari & Stoye (2022, Econometric Theory, arXiv:1908.09103) identify constraint qualifications as hidden geometric assumptions behind partial-identification inference.
Voronin (2025, arXiv:2503.14940) obtains pointwise Gaussian LP-value inference but proves unrestricted uniform consistency impossible.
CCKK (2022, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1912.10529), Lopes–Lin–Müller (2020, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1807.04429), and Vijaykumar (2026, arXiv:2605.29066) supply Gaussian-max coupling and increasingly scale-robust anti-concentration, but not relative critical-value transfer under collapse of the entire envelope scale.
